speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many Singaporeans aged 60 and above have been retrenched, or did not have their contracts renewed, as fallout from the economic impact of COVID-19; (b) how will the Ministry address the challenges of ageism in the COVID-19 economy; and (c) whether the Ministry will provide additional assistance to help seniors who are seeking employment opportunities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, retrenchments have risen and exceeded the peak observed in the SARS outbreak of 2003 but are still lower than during the Global Financial Crisis of 2009.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the first half of 2020, the incidence of local retrenchment was 4.9 per 1,000 local employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the question by Mr Yip Hon Weng, the incidence of local retrenchment for senior workers aged 60 and above was generally comparable, at 5.2 per 1,000 local employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for employees on fixed-term contracts, they constitute about 8% of all employees in the workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The number of contracts not renewed in the first half of 2020 has remained stable compared to the second half of 2019.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MOM does not have data on non-renewals of contracts by age groups.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the question by Ms Sylvia Lim, the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment – which I will henceforth refer to as the Tripartite Advisory – this emphasises retrenchment as a last resort, only after employers have exhausted non-wage-related and wage-related cost-savings measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The advisory sets out expectations for employers when they have to retrench staff.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The main goal of the retrenchment must be to give the business the best chance of survival or continued long-term viability, without which both the employer and all employees are worse-off, even if they were not retrenched.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Selection of employees to be retrenched should be based on objective criteria, with primary considerations given to employee merit and preserving skills to help the business keep going.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, the Tripartite Advisory calls on employers to maintain a strong Singaporean Core even as they retrench.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Tripartite Advisory calls on employers to maintain a strong Singaporean Core even as they retrench.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Based on MOM's investigation of retrenchment cases, businesses have generally taken heed of the advice and made serious efforts to retain Singaporeans in their workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where retrenchments cannot be avoided, WSG will reach out to offer job assistance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In unionised companies, NTUC has sought to minimise their period of unemployment through its "lift and place" efforts, partnering with the Government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A good example is how Singapore crew members from SIA were helped to take up jobs in healthcare with funding support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Beyond efforts to help them stay in work which I will say more about later, Singaporeans also get extra support in social policies, such as education, training and healthcare.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Schemes like Workfare and Silver Support, which help to boost incomes during work and in retirement, apply only to citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Tripartite Advisory that Ms Lim asked about also stipulates that the prevailing norm is to pay a retrenchment benefit of between two weeks' and one month's salary per year of service, depending on the financial position of the company and industry practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the questions by Mr Louis Chua, the requirement to submit retrenchment notifications to MOM covers about 90% of the workforce and provides a broadly representative view.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even amongst employees who were not eligible, almost half received some retrenchment payout.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question of whether a baseline retrenchment benefit should be legislated is not new and has also been debated in Parliament.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The tripartite consensus, after extensive deliberation, is that it does not guarantee better outcomes for retrenched employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The legislated baseline would likely become the default.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even when employers can afford to pay more, they would be unlikely to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the other hand, setting a high baseline retrenchment benefit would strain the financial health of businesses that are already struggling, and potentially jeopardise their survival and the jobs of the remaining employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With legislated retrenchment benefit, employers would also be less likely to offer long-term or permanent contracts to employees, and resort more to hiring employees on short-term contracts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, while recognising the usefulness of retrenchment benefit and encouraging employers to pay according to the prevailing norms, we are even more focused on helping retrenched workers return to the workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides heavy subsidies for skills programmes, we provide substantial training and wage support to employers while their new hires undergo conversion programmes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During this period where hiring sentiments have weakened, we have significantly enhanced the support to local jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We introduced the Jobs Growth Incentive to spur employers to expand local hiring, with double the support for new hires aged 40 and above.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We created the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme to help mid-career locals gain relevant work experience through attachments hosted by companies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will position them to take up jobs later.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have also expanded the SGUnited Skills programme which offers full-time training programmes ranging from six to 12 months.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Yip asked about the additional help for seniors who wish to continue working.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For many decades, we have recognised employers' concerns about the cost of hiring and retaining them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With encouragement from the tripartite partners, many employers have therefore moved away from a seniority-based wage system to competency- or performance-based wage systems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Senior workers aged above 55 years have lower employer CPF contribution rates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government further provides the Special Employment Credit to employers to offset wages of Singaporeans aged 55 and above.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Employers who redesign jobs to be better suited for senior workers can tap on the Productivity Solutions Grant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In more recent times, we observed that senior workers increasingly prefer to reduce their work intensity as they approach retirement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Through these measures, we have made good gains in senior employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During this period of economic uncertainty, the unemployment rate for locals aged 60 and over remains comparable to that of the overall workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nonetheless, MOM recognises Mr Yip's concerns about ageism, especially in a slack job market.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Singapore's employment laws protect employees against discriminatory employment practices, including wrongful dismissal on grounds of age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In January this year, we also strengthened the Fair Consideration Framework for greater deterrence against all forms of workplace discrimination by raising administrative penalties across the board.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our seniors are important and are valued members of our workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to look out for them and support their employers' efforts to retain them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Until the economy recovers more fully, we will maintain the stance of heightened vigilance on the job situation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where retrenchment can be avoided through cost-cutting measures, we will keep a lookout for instances where the wage cuts cause excessive hardship to workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In cases where MOM has intervened, employers that have the means have shown willingness to moderate their wage cuts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where retrenchments cannot be avoided, we will watch out for Singaporeans, give full support to employers' efforts to retain them or to help them move into new jobs as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), Written Answers to Question Nos 22-36 and 39-53 on the Order Paper are reproduced in the Appendix.
